scope_note: Second-pass direct-evidence audit for Meta's Prineville data-center campus at 735 SW Connect Way in Prineville, Crook County. The selected IM3 entity is the campus, not one PRN building, every Vitesse-owned county parcel, Apple's separate campus, or Meta's statewide and global portfolios. The fragment now separates annual company-level potential additional tax from facility-level 2024-25 exemption values, taxable Vitesse totals from exempt account values, billed tax from payment status, agreement schedules from realized distributions, and one exact permit valuation from construction expenditure. Business Oregon identifies all three long-term-rural-zone facilities; Crook County's public assessor portal resolves 25 current Vitesse/Meta accounts across nine map-tax-lot strings and provides an annual history for exact-address account 19380; and Oregon ePermitting supplies an exact permit, contractor, project description and job value. Projections remain projections, overlapping summary/detail tax records are not summed, and multi-company budgets are not allocated. Realized Meta-only PILOT distributions, a reconciled all-account exemption roll, construction payroll/job-years, supplier payments/local-spend share, same-scope public-service costs, campus water bills, and causal county effects remain unavailable.

sources.title: City of Prineville letter on Facebook Prineville Data Center Project
sources.notes: Mayor-authored legislative record summarizing an ECONorthwest analysis for January 2010 through December 2011. It reports approximately $210.4 million in project capital costs to date and 55 Facebook and contract employees. The same letter reports nearly $3.3 million in payroll and estimates geographic spending and wider economic effects, but those figures lack compatible direct metrics or are source-modeled effects and are not added as canonical records.

sources.title: 2011 Economic Revitalization Team Biennial Report
sources.publisher: State of Oregon Economic Revitalization Team
sources.notes: Page 31 describes Facebook's purchase of the remaining certified acreage, a 200,000-square-foot first complex, expected first- and second-phase completion in 2011 and 2012, 250-plus construction jobs, 35-50 permanent-job projections, a 15-year long-term enterprise-zone agreement approved in late 2009, and Oregon Investment Advantage approval. These contemporaneous values are retained as boundary and forecast context rather than duplicated as quantitative records where later or more specific evidence is available.

sources.title: Facebook Launches Open Compute Project
sources.notes: Operator announcement identifies Prineville as Facebook's first dedicated data center and documents that the facility was operating when the Open Compute Project launched. It also reports an initial PUE of 1.07 and comparative efficiency claims, which are not contribution-account amounts and have no matching direct metric.

sources.title: Planning Commission Decision for Facebook property zone change, 735 Connect Way
sources.notes: The decision identifies 735 Connect Way, map and tax lot 1515000000311, the 119.5-acre pre-partition site annexed in 2009, and the parcel between Tom McCall Road and SE Connect Way as the data-center location. It is used to bound the original development, not as proof that the later campus remains a single parcel.

sources.title: Meta Prineville Data Center project profile
sources.notes: General-contractor project profile identifies DPR as contractor for the original campus build and describes the initial scope as two 300,000-square-foot data halls plus a 70,000-square-foot administrative building. It documents contractor identity and physical scope but no contract value, vendor payment, worker residence, payroll or job-years.

sources.title: Investing in Small Business Success in Central Oregon
sources.notes: Operator release states that the first custom-built Prineville data center opened in 2011, two additional buildings had been announced to bring total campus footprint above 3.2 million square feet, the additional investment was $750 million, 100 new jobs were expected, and operations already supported 350 jobs in the region. Future investment and jobs remain projections.

sources.title: Our Prineville Data Center is growing again!
sources.notes: Operator announcement describes a planned 900,000-square-foot, two-building expansion that would produce an 11-building, nearly 4.6-million-square-foot campus and more than $2 billion of investment at completion. It also announces a $60,000 Crook County School District robotics grant and says total Facebook support for the program had reached $150,000. The future-completion values are projections; the two community figures overlap.

sources.title: Property Tax Incentives Impact Study
sources.notes: Page 30 reports that Facebook paid $2.5 million in system development charges to the City of Prineville plus $500,000 in permitting and planning fees to the City and Crook County, and projects that a 5.5% utility franchise fee will equal $1 million annually at full buildout. The report does not date the payments, disaggregate the $500,000 by jurisdiction, or provide a same-scope public-cost ledger.

sources.title: Oregon Business Development Commission June 2023 materials packet
sources.notes: Page 54 states that three Facebook facilities and two Apple facilities in Prineville were then receiving 15-year long-term rural enterprise-zone abatements. It reports $153 million of 2022-23 property-tax impact and $9.3 billion of capital investment for ten data centers across Crook, Morrow and Wasco counties; neither aggregate can be allocated to Meta Prineville.

sources.title: Evaluation and Transparency of Incentives and Loans
sources.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State Audits Division
sources.notes: Page 15 describes high exemption-per-job values for data centers and uses Facebook Prineville as an example, but only publishes a cross-project range and program totals. It does not disclose a Meta-Prineville-specific annual abatement value suitable for a project record.

sources.title: Meta 2023 Sustainability Report
sources.notes: PDF page 51 reports Prineville facility electricity consumption for 2017-2022. The 2017-2019 values extend the direct series; 2020-2022 values are superseded for this fragment by the later 2025 index and are not duplicated.

sources.title: OSU-Cascades Innovation Co-Lab will support minority entrepreneurs with new Blue Fund program
sources.notes: Recipient-authored page verifies a $10,000 gift from the Facebook Prineville Data Center for the Blue Fund program serving underserved entrepreneurs in Crook, Deschutes and Jefferson counties. The regional beneficiary scope is preserved and not represented as Crook County-only funding.

sources.title: Part A — Enterprise Zone Business Projects, 2025 Exemptions on Qualified Property
sources.notes: Official open-data table was queried through its Socrata API and cross-checked with 2023 and 2024 Part A datasets using Crook, Prineville, Facebook and Meta. The Crook County rows are standard-enterprise-zone businesses unrelated to Meta; the table does not supply the three long-term-rural-zone Facebook facility values identified in the 2023 commission packet.

sources.title: Crook County Adopted Budget Fiscal Year 2024
sources.notes: County budget identifies data-center PILOT collections and distributions as special-payment pass-throughs and discusses future replacement by property taxes. Published totals combine data centers and recipients and do not provide a Meta-only cash-receipt series or matching service-cost series.

sources.title: Deschutes Basin water market scoping and planning analysis
sources.notes: Page 24 states that Facebook used groundwater outside Prineville's municipal water-supply system and distinguishes Apple's municipal infrastructure investment from Facebook's then-more-limited water-offset activity. sources.title: Ordinance No. 1234 — Vitesse development, water and sewer service agreement
sources.notes: Approves a negotiated Development, Water and Sewer Service Agreement for Vitesse's planned additional data-center development. The posted ordinance does not include meter data, rates, annual bills or the full executed agreement.

sources.title: Resolution No. 1393 — amended Vitesse project-fee allocation agreement
sources.notes: Resolution, Amendment No. 1 and Exhibit A identify the 2009, 2015 and 2017 Facebook agreements and schedule annual project fees of $110,000 for PRN1-3, $190,000 for PRN4 and $750,000 for PRN5-6. The recitals say the 2017 agreement originally used $250,000; Exhibit A reflects the later amended schedule. Allocation tables combine Facebook and Apple and include future estimated facilities, so only the named Facebook agreement schedules are retained as projections, not receipts. The official resolution detail page still listed this attachment when reviewed, but live attachment navigation on 2026-09-06 returned the City's item-no-longer-available page; the indexed official PDF content is retained with this access limitation.

sources.title: OPUC Order No. 19-238, UM 1989
sources.notes: Order records Vitesse's December 12, 2018 application to exceed PacifiCorp/Pacific Power's new-large-load direct-access cap and grants its July 2019 withdrawal because the waiver was no longer necessary. It does not disclose campus load, power bill or infrastructure cost.

sources.title: OPUC Order No. 21-090, UE 374

project_updates.title: Boundary audit — original 119.5 acres separated from 25 current Vitesse accounts
project_updates.notes: City Ordinance 1182 identifies original map-tax-lot 1515000000311, 119.5 acres, and a three-parcel partition. On 2026-09-06 the public Assessor portal https://pso.crookcountyor.gov/pso was queried by Name=VITESSE across result pages 1-3; it returned 25 current accounts, four personal and 21 real, under VITESSE LLC or META PLATFORMS INC DBA VITESSE LLC, spanning nine displayed map-tax-lot strings. Exact-address account 19380 resolves 735 SW Connect Way to 151501-00-01102 and legal description PP 2010-04 PARCEL 2; related accounts 19271 and 19923 share that tax lot at 511 SW Connect Way. The broader owner result also includes 500 Connect Way, Social Loop, Connect Loop, Houston Lake Road and undetermined/remote holdings, so it is not treated as a campus parcel set. The official deed index at https://clerk.crookcountyor.gov/DigitalResearchRoomPublic/Disclaimer was accessed; County instructions permit only party-name search, not address/map/account/legal-description search, and bot verification blocked an anonymous Vitesse query, while document images are paid. No deed image or current legal-description crosswalk was inferred.
project_updates.project_description: Meta's Prineville Data Center is a Meta-operated campus at 735 Connect Way in Prineville, Crook County, Oregon, not a single building or statewide portfolio. Facebook broke ground in 2010 and launched the first dedicated facility in 2011; City records identify the original 119.5-acre parcel, while contractor records describe two early 300,000-square-foot data halls and a 70,000-square-foot administration building. A March 2021 operator announcement described two planned additions that would bring the campus to 11 buildings and nearly 4.6 million square feet, so those expansion dimensions and the associated investment forecast are kept separate from the original facility.

project_updates.title: Investment audit — three LRZ facility proposals added without relabeling as spend
project_updates.notes: Business Oregon resource re77-krua was queried directly at https://data.oregon.gov/resource/re77-krua.json for certified_business_firm='Vitesse LLC (Facebook)' and DC No. 1, 2 and 3. Proposed investment is $188,168,000, $201,000,000 and $260,175,000, with required minima of $10,450,000, $200,000,000 and $200,000,000; those proposals are retained separately from the approximate $210.4 million through-2011 reported capital cost, the 2018 $750 million expansion forecast and the 2021 greater-than-$2 billion campus-at-completion forecast. Planning, assessor, permit, contractor and operator searches using Facebook, Meta, Vitesse, PRN1-6, capital cost, investment, equipment and assessed/exempt value did not produce an audited annual expenditure ledger, equipment/construction split, current realized cumulative capital or a nonoverlapping phase reconciliation.

project_updates.title: Construction and procurement audit — exact ePermitting record added; ledger remains unreconciled
project_updates.notes: Crook County directs permit-history users to Oregon ePermitting at https://aca-oregon.accela.com/oregon/Cap/CapHome.aspx?module=Building&TabName=Building. Anonymous Building search used 01/01/2009-09/06/2026, street 735, fragment Con and city Prineville and returned 100+ records. Exact record 217-26-000826-STR is Permit Issued for Meta Prineville Fiber Huts / Vitesse, 138 / Fiber hut 07, owned by Vitesse, with Fortis Construction Inc. as applicant/licensed professional and a $140,029.33 job value; it is retained as one permit valuation. Exact-address results also showed electrical, mechanical, fire-revision and void records, demonstrating overlap. Searches of City packets, DPR, Fortis, Rosendin, Mortenson, OSHA and supplier pages using Facebook, Meta, Vitesse, PRN1-6, permit, generator, contractor, subcontractor, supplier, payroll and local spend found identities and scopes but no downloadable all-record ledger, reconciled nonoverlapping construction value, worker hours, job-years, invoices, supplier geography or local-spend share.

project_updates.title: Workforce audit — facility-specific LRZ requirements added; realized payroll still absent
project_updates.notes: Business Oregon resource re77-krua reports required and expected new hires of 35, 10 and 10 for DC No. 1, 2 and 3, with existing job bases of 0, 57 and 99; these are agreement/forecast figures, not realized additions. They remain distinct from 55 Facebook-and-contract employees through 2011, 350 regionally supported jobs reported in 2018, the county's 2023 principal-employer count and the 100-job expansion forecast. Oregon Employment Department/QualityInfo, WorkSource, BOLI apprenticeship and OATS public pages, Meta careers, City/County reports, and contractor pages were searched using Facebook, Meta Platforms, Vitesse, Prineville, employee, contractor, FTE, payroll, salary, occupation, apprenticeship, training agent and local hire for 2010-2026. Public BOLI search did not expose a project/site field or Meta/Vitesse campus result. No current direct-versus-contractor reconciliation, annual payroll, occupation/hours table, employee residence, local-hire realization or project apprenticeship count was found.

project_updates.title: Fiscal and incentive audit — annual abatements, facility values, bills and fee schedules separated
project_updates.notes: Business Oregon resource re77-krua and its 2016-2025 attached composite reports now support ten published Crook County Facebook/Meta potential-additional-tax observations and three facility-level 2024 exempt assessed values: $927,721,260, $571,612,240 and $4,526,256,370. Crook County top-taxpayer PDFs report Vitesse taxable assessed value/tax amount of $10,478,100/$165,478.53 for 2024-25 and $10,314,110/$182,293.11 for 2025-26; these are bills, not payment proof. Assessor account 19380 contributes a separate 2016-2025 exempt-account value history. City Resolutions 1117, 1271 and 1329 establish the three approvals; Resolution 1393 Exhibit A schedules annual project fees of $110,000, $190,000 and amended $750,000 for PRN1-3, PRN4 and PRN5-6. City/County allocation tables mix Facebook, Apple and future estimates, so they are not receipts. The City budget/ACFR, County budget, treasurer payment portal, DOR tax-expenditure/corporate-statistics pages, OIA program page and 2024 DOR central assessment roll were searched using Vitesse/Facebook/Meta, LRZ, PILOT, project fee, payment, distribution and 735 SW Connect Way; the DOR address hit was Zayo centrally assessed telecom property and was excluded. Project-specific SDC and franchise records remain, but no Meta-only cash-payment dates, recipient distributions, account-to-facility crosswalk, compliance certificates, OIA benefit or same-scope public-service cost was published.

project_updates.title: Utility, water and environmental audit — exact dockets and portals documented; water conversion retained
project_updates.notes: OPUC UM 1989 Order 19-238 records Vitesse's 2018 application to exceed Pacific Power's large-load direct-access cap and its 2019 withdrawal; UE 374 Order 21-090 records Vitesse participation concerning Schedule 272. Neither discloses campus kWh, demand, bill or substation cost. OWRD WRIS at https://apps.wrd.state.or.us/apps/wr/wrinfo/ and the 2019 Prineville ASR application/2020 attachment were searched for Vitesse, Facebook, Meta, 735 Connect Way, CROO 53878, G-17089 and G-17236; City rights and ASR permitting appear, but no Vitesse-specific right or annual meter/bill allocation. DEQ's current Your DEQ Online route and pre-November-2024 archive were searched for Vitesse, Facebook, Meta, Prineville and 735 Connect Way; no exact facility air permit or generator inventory surfaced, and the Tier 4 permit is a generic template. EPA facility searches likewise produced no exact campus generator/emissions record. Eight electricity observations remain direct; Meta's rounded 328-megaliter 2024 withdrawal remains only as the single disclosed unit conversion. No tariff assignment, peak demand, IT load, water bill, consumption/discharge, current right allocation, project-funded utility cost, generator count or facility emissions value was found.

project_updates.title: Community audit — recipient confirmations expanded, exact nonoverlapping ledger still absent
project_updates.notes: Meta Community Action Grant pages, Crook County School District board/site search, ORTOP, OSU-Cascades, NeighborImpact, Crook County Kids, Bowman Museum, CASA, libraries and named recipients were searched for 2011-2026 using Facebook, Meta, Prineville, grant, gift, robotics, STEM, nonprofit, school and volunteer. The $60,000 2021 robotics grant, overlapping $150,000 cumulative program support and recipient-verified $10,000 OSU Blue Fund gift remain. NeighborImpact's 2023 Annual Report independently lists Facebook Donations in its $10,000-$24,999 band, but the range and lack of a campus/disbursement date prevent a numeric record. School-district searches confirmed program context but no amount table. Current Meta recipient lists generally state purposes without awards. No complete annual campus grant ledger, payment date, in-kind valuation, volunteer-hour value or Crook-only allocation for regional programs was found.

project_updates.title: Structured-data and modeling audit — county comparison gaps removed; one conversion retained
project_updates.notes: All four prior syntheses were reassessed against the expanded direct register. The three inverse-distance-weighted county GDP, employment and wage gaps were removed: each is noncausal, the 2011 anchor is followed by multiple Meta phases and Apple's separate campus, and the results add no defensible decision value beyond observed county series; the employment fit was especially poor. The only retained synthesis converts Meta's rounded 328-megaliter 2024 Prineville facility withdrawal to gallons with an explicit rounding band because the direct register lacks a compatible annual-water-withdrawal metric. No supplier, construction-employment, payroll, induced-spending, net-fiscal or public-service-cost model is eligible without local-purchase shares, project payroll, recipient alignment and same-scope cost inputs. The newly direct annual LRZ tax-savings series is not modeled. No records requests were made.
